significance.justification: A verified-true result would license a form-(iii) conclusion: belief revision follows an "abrupt threshold" with a source-dependent "hysteresis-gap," and an internal "belief-confidence" quantity predicts how much contradictory evidence will trigger a flip; the steering component is additionally a form-(ii) causal claim. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining expected flip ordering across first-mentioned versus parametric priors, predicting later update failures, and identifying whether stubbornness and over-flipping are opposite settings of one controllable process rather than unrelated errors. MQuAKE (Zhong et al., EMNLP 2023) treats consistent propagation of knowledge updates as an important evaluation target, so failure of the claimed threshold, asymmetry, and predictive coupling would still rule out a unified inertia account, although rejection of the bundled claim would not by itself select one alternative. True and false outcomes are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: deleting the specific threshold, hysteresis, source asymmetry, and predictive coupling leaves only generic research on belief representations, which would not merit this rating.

reach.justification: The claim hands over the named metrics "evidence-flip-count" and "hysteresis-gap," an internal "belief-confidence" predictor, and a "belief-stability" steering intervention. The metrics can diagnose completed update behavior, but the stronger handle is ex ante because the claim says the evidence required for a future flip is "predictable from an internal 'belief-confidence' direction," leaving time to flag or adjust a model before it ignores evidence or over-flips. After per-model re-extraction, the direction itself may change, but the asserted threshold, source-conditioned asymmetry, and confidence-to-flip predictive relation say what should recur across model families; likely downstream users include researchers evaluating knowledge updates and practitioners tuning or auditing stubbornness and sycophancy. The topic-substitution check passes: generic LLM-belief research supplies none of these forecasting metrics or control handles, so the reach comes from this claim rather than from the topic's general importance.
